messages:
sara-support: Escalating from CS — customer `acme-finance` started getting 401s immediately after an API key rotation. They say Vault shows the new key, but their traffic still hitting us with the old key. Attached snippet from their proxy logs and a curl attempt below.

ryan-enginfra: Thanks Sara. Can you paste the original request headers + the first 5 lines of our edge logs for one of the failed requests? suspecting cached token at our CDN/edge layer or a client-side env cache.

sara-support: Uploading logs: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_old_abc123" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` -> 401. Our edge access log shows: `edge-nyc1 10.2.3.4 GET /v1/generate 401 sk_live_old_abc123` and upstream returned 403->converted to 401 by auth layer.

customer-acmeops: Confirmed — we rotated the key in Vault and triggered the CI to redeploy. The app uses an AWS Lambda proxy that reads key from SSM Parameter Store at startup. We restarted the service but might have missed a pool. We're seeing ~5% of traffic with old key, mostly from a batch job.

mike-oncall: Noted. Two quick checks: 1) Is there an edge cache or CDN token cache layer that snaps to API key header? 2) Any pod/instance still running old envvars? Also confirm there isn't an SSO-linked key or token exchange in play.

ryan-enginfra: We don't cache bearer tokens at the CDN permanently, but we do keep a short auth result cache keyed by hashed credential to avoid rate on KMS unwrap when key verified recently. TTL=10m in prod by default. If the old key was valid until immediate revoke, you can get mixed results until caches expire or we force a purge.

sara-support: Customer says they revoked the old key in Vault immediately after issuing new one. Vault shows old key disabled. Also, their Lambda does a warm pool — containers reuse environment variables for multiple invocations. They restarted the main service but maybe the batch worker didn't restart.

customer-acmeops: The batch job runs on a scheduled fleet separate from the web lambda. We rotated the parameter in SSM but forgot to redeploy the batch fleet. We'll restart it now.

deploy-bot: Redeploy started for service `acme-batch-worker` at 2026-03-15T09:34:21Z.

ryan-enginfra: Two follow-ups while they restart: 1) Can support provide a request ID of a failing call so we can check our auth cache entries and edge traces? 2) If they can reproduce with the old key, capture full request headers (including X-Forwarded-For) and response body.

sara-support: Got one failing request ID: `req_2832101507_abcd`. Full trace shows: `auth.check -> unwrap(kms:alias/old-key) -> cache MISS -> verify -> FAIL -> return 401`. But weirdly some traces earlier that minute show `cache HIT` then `verify -> PASS` for the same old key, which suggests a race between revoke and our cache TTL.

mike-oncall: That matches the race. If Vault revocation happened after some edge nodes cached a successful verification result, TTL will keep them returning 200 until expiry. Workarounds: 1) Customer fully restarts all clients (force new connections), 2) We can trigger an auth-cache invalidation for that credential hash from our side.

customer-acmeops: We restarted the batch fleet, but still seeing a few fails. Looks like some traffic goes through a third-party API gateway sitting in front of their batch worker that replays a cached token header. We're coordinating to flush that cache as well.

ryan-enginfra: I'll add a short-term mitigation: schedule an immediate invalidation of auth cache entries that map to the disabled Vault key. I'll need the key fingerprint or last 8 chars. Sara, can you get that from the customer?

sara-support: Provided last 8 chars: `abc12345`.

ryan-enginfra: Done. Invalidated cache for cred-hash `sha256:...abc12345` across edge nodes at 2026-03-15T09:40:02Z. Propagation log: `edge-node-* cache.invalidate(cred-hash) -> ok`.

customer-acmeops: After invalidation and fleet restart, errors dropped to 0. Thank you. A couple of notes for us: our CI needs to trigger full workers restart after SSM param change.

mike-oncall: Good to hear. Follow-ups for postmortem: 1) Add a cache-invalidation API for customers to call on revocation (low-risk auth-only endpoint) 2) Document recommended rotation procedure for serverless fleets and third-party gateways. 3) Evaluate reducing TTL or adding revocation webhook from Vault to invalidate our auth cache automatically.

ryan-enginfra: Agreed on the three items. I'll open tickets: ENGINFRA-1421 (customer-triggered auth-cache invalidate), ENGINFRA-1422 (Vault revocation webhook), DOCS-789 (rotation runbook for serverless + gateways).

sara-support: I'll update the customer with the mitigation steps and link the runbook once DOCS-789 is ready. Closing this thread once customer confirms stable. :white_check_mark:

customer-acmeops: Confirmed stable. Thanks everyone!

mike-oncall: Closing on our side — please reference req_2832101507_abcd in postmortem.

sara-support: closing.
